story.title: The Backup Self
story.logline: A man discovers his deceased wife has been calling his backup clone every single Tuesday.
story.theme: The terrifying duplication of grief and love.
story.twist: The wife did not die in the crash; the husband did, and his clone was activated with false memories.
story.ending: Who answers when you are no longer the one who picked up the phone?

scenes.narration: My dead wife called my phone at midnight, whispering the exact same secret she told me before the crash.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 30, tired eyes, dark messy hair, wearing a worn gray hoodie, holding a glowing smartphone in a dark, minimalist apartment.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on the glowing screen, slow push in.

scenes.narration: I stared at the screen showing her name, Elena, dead for six months, lighting up my pitch-black bedroom.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, sitting rigidly on the edge of a messy bed, staring at the phone.

scenes.narration: My trembling finger pressed accept, expecting silence, but her warm breathing rushed straight through the tiny speaker.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, pressing the phone to his ear with a shaking hand.
scenes.camera: Tight profile shot focusing on his terrified expression.

scenes.narration: You answered faster this week, Leo, she whispered, her voice crisp and clear like she was standing right beside me.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, looking around the empty, dark bedroom in sudden panic.
scenes.camera: Slow pan left to reveal an empty dark hallway.

scenes.narration: I am not Leo, I choked out into the dark. I am the backup copy they activated yesterday.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, tears welling in his eyes as he speaks into the phone.
scenes.camera: Push in on his tearful, panicked face.

scenes.narration: She went quiet on the line. Then she laughed, a cold sound that froze the blood in my veins.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, pulling the phone away from his ear in absolute confusion.

scenes.narration: I know you are the backup, darling, Elena whispered softly. That is why I always call you on Tuesdays.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, eyes wide with sudden realization in the dark room.
scenes.camera: Rapid push in on his terrified eyes.

scenes.narration: The real Leo died in the wreckage. The insurance company only paid for a mind stored in plastic.
scenes.visual_prompt: Medium shot of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, looking down at his glowing hands as if seeing them for the first time.

scenes.narration: She never loved the man who died. She only loved the machine built to replace his absence.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, holding the phone tightly against his cheek, defeated and hollow.
scenes.camera: Slow circular orbit around his head.

scenes.narration: My dead wife called my backup phone tonight, proving some memories are designed to outlive the soul.
scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of Leo, 30, messy hair, gray hoodie, sitting alone in the dark apartment as the phone screen finally goes black.
scenes.camera: Pull back to wide, fading to absolute black.

caption.hook: She calls the dead man every Tuesday.
caption.title: The Backup Self
caption.caption:
He thought he was mourning the love of his life. But every Tuesday at 3 AM, her voice echoes through his cloned reality, whispering secrets meant for a ghost who never existed. Is love still real when the memories are manufactured?

Would you answer the phone?
